# Card 209: task-force declaration proposal (objection window 209-taskforce)

Category: task-force declaration. Proposed by: product manager (ready), claude-sonnet seat, ctx-1 of card 209.
Probe reference: .mob/records/probes/2026-10-30.jsonl (12:03 UTC).

## Task force
- Product manager (ready): Claude | why: refines card 209 at ready; confirms the MD-001 subject token and that the card's ZOMBIES (already in the card) stay as written; applies D157 to the Done checks | context: ctx-1
- Architect (slice): Claude | why: slices the card and numbers its acceptance criteria 1 to 3 before red (D157), with the check-by-layer table (facilitator.py, mob_process.py, template) so both entry points share one refusal text; the card-record checker (schema 1) requires a slice seat | context: ctx-6
- QA engineer (red): Claude | why: turns the card's ZOMBIES into failing tests, one acceptance criterion per red-green cycle (D157), for the refusal in facilitator.py, the same refusal in mob_process.py, and the template and test removal | context: ctx-2
- Backend developer [author] (green, refactor): Claude | why: changes facilitator.py, mob_process.py and templates/TEAM_WORKING_AGREEMENT.default.md in mob-defaults (C:\Users\ringe\mob-crosscli) so each red test passes; deletes the cycle-removal syntax and the test at tests/test_card_mode.py:914 | context: ctx-3
- Independent reviewer (audit lens) [reviewer]: Claude | why: non-author review of the diff against MD-001 and the ruling that removal happens only at the retro; checks both entry points give the same refusal text | context: ctx-4
- Delivery lead (ship): Claude | why: runs the D154 pre-ship gate (trial card 3 of 5) and the CI-on-main check; the checker requires a ship seat with its own commit evidence | context: ctx-7
- Product manager (signoff): Claude | why: a fresh context signs off against the three Done checks, because the refinement seat may not hold the sign-off seat | context: ctx-5

The card record checker (scripts/mob_process.py, schema 1) requires seats for ready, slice, red, green, ship and signoff, each with distinct commit evidence; a card without slice and ship seats cannot be closed. Seven seats cover those six roles plus the independent reviewer.

The reviewer seat is named "Independent reviewer (audit lens)", never "auditor": auditor_seated_problems in mob_process.py refuses any card seat whose role contains "auditor", because the auditor is external to the mob and never seated.

## Left out
UX designer and frontend developer (no interface); database developer (no such code); security (no new trust boundary); DevOps (no workflow, hook or runner change); technical writer (the template edit is a deletion); language and grammar designers (no language change); performance engineer (no hot path); agile coach (no process change beyond the product owner ruling; D157 is applied, not changed); separate Python or facilitator expert (see below).

## Domain expert (refinement)
Should another domain join now? No. The change sits inside facilitator.py, mob_process.py and the template, which the backend developer covers. The reviewer seat, given the audit lens, is the domain check for MD-001 and the no-removal ruling, so the author does not review their own reading of the rule. If the red seat finds the two entry points cannot share one refusal message, any member adds an expert through a Decider (mid-card addition, with the Decider id). Adding is unchanged by this card.

## Reason for Claude seats
Probes at 12:03 UTC (.mob/records/probes/2026-10-30.jsonl) show Codex, Copilot, Grok and agy without usable quota (copilot has_quota=False; grok 402 balance exhausted; agy 429 quota reached). Each seat is a distinct fresh context, and nobody reviews or QAs their own increment (author ctx-3, QA ctx-2, reviewer ctx-4, signoff ctx-5, refinement ctx-1, slice ctx-6, ship ctx-7). Non-Claude models come first again as soon as a fresh probe shows quota.

## D157 applies
One acceptance criterion per red-green cycle, checked from git (5-card experiment, Decider D157):
- The slice (architect, ctx-6) numbers the card's criteria 1 to 3 before any red.
- Each red commit body carries "Criterion: n" (n = the Done check number, 1 to 3).
- The green for criterion n lands before any red for n+1.
- Greens are pushed at once.
- Card 209's ZOMBIES are already in the card for all three Done checks; QA does not rewrite them, only implements them (a ZOMBIES change is a card-text fix through this window).
- Each commit stays within D136 and cites MD-001 and D145 in the subject or body; red first (D137).

## Window rule
- Every declared role is polled (F-054): all seven role seats answer (ready ctx-1 is the proposer; slice ctx-6, red ctx-2, green ctx-3, reviewer ctx-4, ship ctx-7, signoff ctx-5), each in its own fresh context.
- Each seat answers either "no objection" or ONE fixed condition per objection (D145). A condition that is simply adopted and re-polled stays in the window; an unsettled objection goes to a full Decider.
- Card-text changes proposed with this declaration are card-text fixes in the same window (D153).

## Why this is neither a one-way door nor a standing-rule change
Two-way door: the declaration ends with the card and can be re-declared; nothing is published, deleted or migrated. It applies TFDD and D157 as written and changes no agreement, D-record or checker. (The card itself changes the checker, but that is the card's work under its own Done checks, not this declaration.)

---
